Bayesian model comparison favours a refreshed two-component jet scenario

findings_qualitative.value: The host-galaxy association is ambiguous between an offset LS DR10 galaxy candidate (objid 5790 at 33.51 kpc) and an undetected fainter near-coincident galaxy below the LS DR10 threshold.

evidence.quote: The host association is ambiguous: the nearest LS DR10 galaxy candidate ($r_{\rm AB}\sim24.7$) is offset by $\sim4\ensuremath{''}$ ($\sim34$ kpc) with chance-alignment probability $P_{\rm cc}\sim0.2$, and current imaging does not exclude a fainter, near-coincident host.

claims.hypothesis: The broadband afterglow of GRB 250818B requires additional dynamical structure (energy injection and/or angular structure) beyond a standard single-component top-hat forward shock.
claims.experiment: Perform nested-sampling inference with nessai comparing a single-component top-hat jet model (afterglowpy) against a refreshed-shock two-component jet model (twocomponent_redback_refreshed in redback) across X-ray, optical, and radio data.
claims.result: The top-hat model mismatches the X-ray light curve after 0.02 d, underpredicts late-time (>3 d) optical and 36.8 GHz emission, and pushes against the p=2 prior boundary; the refreshed two-component model is preferred with ln Bayes = 42.537 and yields p = 1.64 +/- 0.05.
claims.finding: Departures from the simplest single-component forward shock—specifically refreshed-shock energy injection and a two-component jet structure with p < 2—are strongly preferred to explain the broadband evolution.

evidence.quote: Bayesian model comparison prefers the refreshed two-component model over the single-component top-hat fit (Table [\[tab:pri_post\]](#tab:pri_post)), supporting the interpretation that additional dynamical structure (energy injection and/or angular stratification) is a required feature of this GRB afterglow.

claims.hypothesis: The afterglow of the nominal short GRB 250818B is unusually luminous compared to the short-GRB population across X-ray, optical, and radio bands.
claims.experiment: Measure the spectroscopic redshift with Keck/LRIS and compare the Swift/XRT, optical R-band, and radio (MeerKAT/VLA/ALMA) light curves and luminosities against literature short- and long-GRB populations.
claims.result: At z = 1.216, the early X-ray flux is brighter than 96-99% of Swift short GRBs, the optical R-band afterglow at 0.3-0.9 d is 2.7-3.0 mag brighter than the short/Type I median (brighter than 93-97% of Type I afterglows), and it is only the third short GRB with a radio detection at z > 1.
claims.finding: GRB 250818B lies on the bright tail of the short-GRB afterglow distribution across X-rays, optical, and radio, while being typical of long GRBs in X-ray/optical brightness.

evidence.quote: GRB 250818B is only the third short GRB to have a detected radio afterglow at $z > 1$, with the other two short GRBs being GRB 170728B (cite: 2022ApJ...940...56F) and GRB 210726A (cite: 2024ApJ...970..139S).

evidence.loc: Progenitor interpretation: merger versus collapsar contamination
evidence.quote: At these times, GRB 250818B is brighter than $\approx 96$–$99\%$ of the Swift short-duration sample ($N_{\rm short}=35$–$47$), but brighter than only $\approx 67$–$73\%$ of the Swift long-duration sample ($N_{\rm long}=994$–$1041$).

claims.hypothesis: The nearest catalogued LS DR10 galaxy (objid 5790) can be definitively associated as the host galaxy of GRB 250818B, allowing offset-based progenitor classification.
claims.experiment: Calculate empirical chance-coincidence probabilities (P_cc), Bayesian host association probabilities (including an uncatalogued/faint host term), and local LS DR10 detection limits at the afterglow position.
claims.result: Candidate objid 5790 (offset by 4.03 arcsec or 33.51 kpc) has P_cc = 0.195 and Bayesian P_assoc = 0.025, while the probability of an uncatalogued host is P_empty = 0.882 (P_faint = 0.829) down to the local 3-sigma galaxy limit r = 24.61.
claims.finding: The host association is tentative and ambiguous because current imaging cannot exclude a fainter near-coincident host below the LS DR10 threshold, limiting offset-based arguments to distinguish between a merger and a collapsar origin.

evidence.quote: Thus, within the LS DR10 catalogue and in this framework, we cannot definitely identify that `objid` 5790 is the true host and instead find support for the host being outside of the galaxy catalogue, $P_{\varnothing} \approx 0.882$, where we find that $P_{\rm out} \approx 0.084$ and $P_{\rm faint} \approx 0.829$.

At the same time, the imaging depth does not exclude a fainter, near-coincident host below the LS DR10 detection threshold, which would reduce the true physical offset and weaken offset-based classification arguments.

why_this_data.value: Because public prompt-emission constraints are limited and host association is uncertain, broadband multi-wavelength follow-up (including low- and high-frequency radio/mm) is needed to anchor the synchrotron spectrum and constrain the explosion energetics and environment.

evidence.quote: Because these scenarios imply very different physical offsets (and therefore limit the use of offset-based arguments), we place particular emphasis on constraints that arise directly from the broadband afterglow data.
In particular, when prompt-emission constraints are weak or unavailable, the afterglow becomes the primary handle on the explosion energetics and environment.

why_this_method.value: A refreshed two-component jet model was used because the baseline single-component top-hat model failed to reproduce the X-ray evolution and late-time optical/radio excess; an XRT-informed beta prior was used in optical SED fitting to break the beta-A_V degeneracy across three bands.

evidence.quote: To reduce the strong $\beta$–$A_V$ degeneracy inherent to three-band photometry, we incorporate an X-ray-informed prior on $\beta$.

A single-component top-hat jet provides a reasonable overall fit but does not reproduce the full evolution: it exhibits a noticeable mismatch to the X-ray light curve from $\sim 0.02$ d, underpredicts the optical emission at $\gtrsim 3$ d, and underpredicts the 36.8 GHz detection at $\sim 4$ – $5$ d (noting the large uncertainty on this point).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: More complex X-ray spectral models (rejected because the simple absorbed power-law model gave CSTAT/DoF = 0.24 with no systematic residuals and limited photon statistics).

evidence.quote: The absorbed power-law model provides an adequate description of the data (CSTAT/DoF = 0.24), with no systematic residuals; given the limited photon statistics, we therefore do not explore more complex spectral models.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: M14/LMC dust extinction law for the optical afterglow SED (rejected because it is undefined below rest-frame 3000 Angstrom, which is probed by observed g and r bands at z = 1.216).

evidence.quote: We do not consider the M14/LMC family further because it is undefined below $\lambda_{\rm rest}\sim3000$ Å, whereas at $z=1.216$ the observed $g$ and $r$ bands probe $\lambda_{\rm rest}\lesssim3000$ Å.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Joint optical+X-ray SED fits at t = 2 d with fixed cooling-break slope difference (rejected as baseline because the 1 keV X-ray point at 2 d is only marginal and introduces extra assumptions that dominate weak constraints).

evidence.quote: However, at $t\simeq2$ d the contemporaneous 1 keV flux is only a marginal detection and does not meet the quality cuts adopted for our X-ray analysis.
We therefore adopt the optical-only fit with the XRT-informed $\beta$ prior as our baseline.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-component top-hat forward-shock model and reverse-shock component for late variability (rejected because the top-hat model is disfavoured by Bayesian model comparison and excess emission occurs after the afterglow peak, ruling out a reverse shock).

evidence.quote: Bayesian model comparison prefers the refreshed two-component model over the single-component top-hat fit
as the excess emission is seen at times later than the afterglow peak, we can rule out any reverse shock component for the afterglow variability.

limitations_admitted.value: Public prompt-emission constraints are limited (Fermi/GBM was in the SAA, and nominal short-GRB classification relies on SVOM discovery notices).

evidence.quote: We inspected the publicly available *Fermi*/GBM time-tagged event (TTE) data around $T_{0}$ and found that the spacecraft appears to have been traversing the South Atlantic Anomaly at that time; accordingly, no on-board or ground trigger was reported.
Public prompt-emission constraints are limited, so we adopt the nominal short-GRB classification reported in discovery notices

limitations_admitted.value: The 10 GHz VLA measurement from GCN 41455 had no reported uncertainty, requiring an assumed uncertainty for modelling.

evidence.quote: In addition, we include the 10 GHz flux density reported in GCN 41455 (cite: Ricci2025gcn41455). As no uncertainty was provided, the point is shown as indicative in Fig. 2; for modelling, we assign an assumed uncertainty to prevent the fit from being dominated by this measurement.

limitations_admitted.value: Host-frame afterglow extinction A_V^host is weakly constrained by only three photometric points (1 dof) and is sensitive to host-subtraction and cross-calibration systematics.

evidence.quote: Given that the fit is constrained by only three photometric points (one degree of freedom) and is sensitive to host-subtraction and cross-calibration systematics, these numerical values should be regarded as indicative rather than definitive.

limitations_admitted.value: In the refreshed two-component jet model, microphysical parameters (epsilon_e, epsilon_B, xi_N) and viewing angle (theta_obs = 0) are fixed, so inferred energetics and density are conditional on these assumed values.

evidence.quote: The normalisation of this illustrative curve (and the implied energy/density scalings) should therefore be regarded as conditional on the assumed microphysical parameters.
In the refreshed two-component model, the microphysics are fixed

limitations_admitted.value: Host galaxy association is ambiguous because LS DR10 imaging depth does not rule out a fainter near-coincident host, and Prospector SED results suffer from age-dust-metallicity degeneracies due to limited UV/NIR detections.

evidence.quote: Given the limited UV/blue and NIR leverage (no deep $u/v$ detection and only mid-IR limits), the age–dust–metallicity degeneracy remains significant and propagates into the posterior uncertainties in $\log Z_\star$ and $\mathrm{sSFR}_{100\,\mathrm{Myr}}$.

At the same time, the imaging depth does not exclude a fainter, near-coincident host below the LS DR10 detection threshold, which would reduce the true physical offset and weaken offset-based classification arguments.

referee_caveats_inferred: The Bayes factor comparison between the single-component top-hat model and the refreshed two-component model uses different parameter spaces and prior ranges (e.g., fixing epsilon_e, epsilon_B, xi_N, and theta_obs in the two-component model while allowing p < 2 only in the two-component model), which directly affects the marginal likelihoods.
The short-GRB classification is taken solely from preliminary GCN notices without published SVOM T90 or spectral hardness measurements in the paper.

data_public_as_stated.value: All compiled photometric, X-ray, and radio datasets are tabulated in the paper; additional data available upon reasonable request.

evidence.quote: All data sets supporting this study are provided in the paper. Additional data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

products_in_archive.value: ALMA QA2 final image products were downloaded directly from the ALMA science archive (Program 2024.1.01131.T).

evidence.quote: We downloaded the final image products from the ALMA science archive. In the Quality Assurance Level 2 (QA2) images, no significant emission is seen in a $0.5\ensuremath{''}$ circle at the GOTO position.
